subject: POC environment playbook - stepwise MAP for API keys, org setup, IP allowlist & peering
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@novamed-health.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff & MAP — what we need from Redwood

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers. We want to lock in a mutual action plan and a concrete day-zero checklist for our POC. High level asks from our infra/devops side:
- API key provisioning and least-privilege org setup for Novamed engineers
- IP allowlist for outbound requests from our app to Redwood API (we're on GCP)
- Optional VPC peering if we need private connectivity (we prefer peering if it avoids NAT egress)
- A short schedule for evaluation milestones and a close window (we aim to decide by end of month)

Can you send a step-by-step MAP (including who owns each item, expected lead times, and any docs/attachments)? Also looping in our infra lead Ryan (ryan.brown@novamed-health.com).

Best,
Anna Li
CTO, Novamed Health


From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@novamed-health.com>, Ryan Brown <ryan.brown@novamed-health.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & MAP — what we need from Redwood

Anna — thanks, glad the demo landed. Attached is a lightweight MAP workbook and a short playbook tailored for Novamed (redwood_map_template_v1.xlsx). Below is the stepwise plan we propose (owners and tentative lead times). If this looks good we can lock dates.

1) Contract & access baseline (Owner: Sales / Monica) — 1 business day after signature
   - Sign trial agreement / PO (Doc links in HubSpot)
   - Create org space for Novamed in Redwood console

2) API keys & least-privilege roles (Owner: Monica + Grace) — 1 business day after org created
   - Create two API keys: "novamed-internal" (full inference) and "novamed-readonly" (monitoring)
   - Share secure link to keys and rotation guidance

3) Network preflight: IP allowlist vs. Peering (Owner: Engineering / Vivek + Novamed infra) — 3-5 business days to validate
   - If using allowlist: provide static egress IP ranges (we'll supply CIDRs)
   - If peering: schedule VPC peering, exchange project IDs, route tables, and CIDRs

4) Service accounts & service-catalog mapping (Owner: Novamed + Marcus) — 2 business days
   - Recommend a dedicated service account for inference calls; create RBAC mapping in org

5) Smoke tests & acceptance criteria (Owner: Novamed + Redwood) — 1-2 days
   - Request set of 5 representative prompts/throughput profile to validate latency and correctness

6) Close review & decision (Owner: Exec sponsors) — target date: 2026-09-30

I've flagged a couple of technical questions to Vivek below — Vivek, can you confirm expected egress CIDR list and whether peering requires shared VPC support? Marcus and Grace, please add any missing items.

Attachments: redwood_map_template_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), novamed_network_details.pdf (Novamed network notes received)

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@novamed-health.com>, Ryan Brown <ryan.brown@novamed-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & MAP — network and peering details

Quick technical notes to help Novamed choose path and timeline:

- Egress IPs (allowlist): For hosted Redwood API we can provide a stable set of 6 IPv4 CIDR ranges; these are NAT egress addresses from our regional edge. Typical setup: add those CIDRs to your outbound allowlist for the POC. Lead time: immediate once we confirm region (US-Central vs US-West) — 1 business day to confirm ranges.

- VPC peering: We support GCP VPC peering. Requirements:
  * Exchange project IDs and VPC names (Novamed provides)
  * Agree on CIDR ranges that do not overlap (Novamed provides full VPC CIDR)
  * Configure route-exports/imports and update firewall rules to allow 443/TCP egress to Redwood subnets
  * Peering build typically takes 2-4 business days (includes validation & route propagation)

- Recommendation: Start with allowlist for the first 48 hours of the POC to move fast. If you need guaranteed lower egress latency or private traffic, schedule peering as a parallel task (kickoff within 48 hours).

- API key + service account flow: We'll create keys scoped to your org; if you prefer, we can mint keys tied to a Redwood service account mapped to your Novamed email group. Keys must be rotated; see section in attached MAP.

- Logging & audit: If you need extended request logs for the POC, let us know retention and we will enable a dedicated trace stream (note: extra cost if >30 days).

I'll prepare the CIDRs for US-West and US-Central and post them to the shared Drive link by EOD.

— Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@novamed-health.com>, Ryan Brown <ryan.brown@novamed-health.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff & MAP — service account and testing cadence

Adding a few engineering specifics and a proposed test window:

- Service account & rate limits: We recommend creating a single service account for the POC with quota cap of 20 rps and burst up to 40 for short load tests. If you expect heavier sustained throughput, tell us and we'll propose Dedicated config.

- Test plan (suggested):
  1) Day 0: API key issuance + allowlist applied -> basic smoke tests (5 prompts)
  2) Day 1: Throughput test (ramp to 20 rps, 10 minutes) + accuracy check
  3) Day 3: If peering in progress, validate private connectivity and run the same tests over peered path

- Input required from Novamed:
  * Public-facing egress CIDRs or confirmation that you want peering (include project IDs and host VPC CIDR)
  * List of 5 representative prompts and size payloads

I'll reserve a 2-hour engineering slot on 2026-09-06 for the smoke + throughput test; please confirm.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
